newsitem.title: USA: US foreign crudes quiet, but Cusiana bids restart.
newsitem.headline: US foreign crudes quiet, but Cusiana bids restart.

text.p: The foreign crude scene among U.S. traders was light on action Tuesday in a market featuring more offers than bidding, traders said.
"I don't know if it's just buyers laying back but it doesn't look too good for physicals right now," said one trader. "I think there's a lot of crude out there."

But traders said Ecopetrol was accepting bids on its second Cusiana tender for June 17-18 loading, just after selling an end-June cargo of the light sweet crude to an East Coast refiner at a $1.20-$1.23 discount to July WTI/Cushing.
They said they expected Ecopetrol to announce the winner of the next tender either late Tuesday or by Wednesday.
Also, players narrowed in on the price British Petroleum fetched for its June 21-22 cargo, saying a midwestern refiner paid $1.23 under July WTI/Cushing.
In other Colombian action, traders said a European oil company picked up Ecopetrol's tender for Vasconia crude loading around June 23-30, though the price was not known.
Word had it the European player had speculative intentions, hoping to turn around and sell it at a profit, traders said.
But that may be difficult in the nearer-term, since sellers seem to be outnumbering buyers.
On Tuesday, players said the focus on expiry of June crude on the NYMEX kept some of buying interest out of the physical market.
"It's been real quiet. Everyone was concentrating on the Merc," said another trader.

Traders were reluctant to characterize the market as "sloppy," saying the lull in action is focused on near-term arrivals and the interest on more deferred supplies should prove to be anything but bearish.
"There's certainly no shortage, but I wouldn't call it sloppy," another trader said.
In other market talk, a West Coast refiner was pegged as the buyer of a Stasco Nigerian Bonny Light cargo sold last week for arrival in the U.S. Gulf June 1, traders said.
They said that West Coast player was said to be interested in delivering the cargo into the NYMEX screen for June deliveries.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1633
